findings.finding: The port cannot be imported: the §1-sanctioned runtime deps are not declared or installed, yet the reviewed files import them. pyproject.toml line 5 declares `dependencies = []`; uv.lock contains no httpx/beautifulsoup4/mcp; .venv site-packages contains neither httpx nor bs4 (only mypy/ruff/pytest). Both cloud service.py files do `import httpx` (websearch line 18, webfetch line 14) and postprocessor.py lines 12-13 do `from bs4 import ...`. Rulebook §1 'Third-party deps' row: 'runtime: mcp, httpx, beautifulsoup4' — the sanctioned deps must exist for the code to even import; nothing in the deviation log waives this.
findings.citation: RULEBOOK §1 row 'Third-party deps'; pyproject.toml:5 `dependencies = []`; uv.lock (no httpx/bs4/mcp); .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages listing

findings.finding: §0's in-loop referee cannot have passed, and §7 logs nothing. §0: 'Every translated unit must pass make lint typecheck (ruff + mypy strict) before it counts as drafted.' Makefile:9-10 runs `uv run mypy .`; pyproject [tool.mypy] strict=true with no ignore_missing_imports; the three reviewed files carry 8 cross-module imports that resolve to modules absent from src/ (see next finding), so mypy fails with unresolved-import errors on every one. Both cloud files are nonetheless trailered `PORT STATUS: confidence=high`. The §7 deviation log (DEV-001..DEV-004) has no entry for skipping/waiving the referee — 'a deviation nobody logged is a deviation nobody approved'.
findings.citation: RULEBOOK §0 ('must pass make lint typecheck before it counts as drafted') and §7 (table ends at DEV-004); Makefile:9-10; pyproject.toml:17-21 ([tool.mypy] strict, exclude only migration/)

findings.finding: Module wiring is unresolvable per the §4 module map: every non-stdlib, non-httpx import in the batch points at a manifest-listed target that does not exist under src/. webfetch/cloud/service.py imports websearch.services.network.client, websearch.services.webfetch.service, ...webfetch.cloud.output, ...webfetch.cloud.parameters; websearch/cloud/service.py imports websearch.services.network.client, websearch.services.websearch.service, ...websearch.cloud.output, ...websearch.cloud.parameters; postprocessor.py imports websearch.services.webfetch.local.postprocessor.postprocessor. None of these 8 files exist (only the 3 reviewed modules + scaffold main.py 'Hello from websearch' are on disk). Consequence for my batch: the 'decode zero-value semantics incl. raise-on-non-list results' site is delegated (websearch service.py:141 `Output.from_response(resp.json())`) to a module that is not written — the websearch WIRE-DECODE row's decision (missing/null results -> []; non-list raises; non-dict element -> zero row; raw content span via raw_decode) exists only on paper, and the URL-JOIN rows' mandatory unit-test matrix is also absent (tests/ has only test_placeholder.py).
findings.citation: RULEBOOK §4 (internal/<path>.go -> src/websearch/<path>.py); manifest.tsv rows 2-5, 15, 19-21 (client.py, webfetch/service.py, websearch/service.py, 2x cloud/output.py, 2x cloud/parameters.py, postprocessor/postprocessor.py); inventory.tsv WIRE-DECODE row websearch/cloud/output.go; URL-JOIN row 'PIN with a unit test over the Go probe matrix'

findings.finding: Silent Go-semantics gap in snippet_from_content: Go's json.Unmarshal matches struct field names case-insensitively (encoding/json/decode.go:700-703 — `fields.byExactName`, then `fields.byFoldedName[string(foldName(key))]`), so wire content `{"Text":"hi"}` makes Go return "hi"; the port's exact-key `parsed.get("text")` (lines 173-175) returns the raw span '{"Text":"hi"}' instead (probed: impl('{"Text":"hi"}') = '{"Text":"hi"}', Go = 'hi'). Neither the code comment (which claims 'isinstance + non-empty mirrors both') nor the snippetFromContent inventory row decides this — an unlisted construct that per §2 'a reviewer who sees an unlisted construct flags it for this table'. Unjudged today: judge s02/fixture linkup.json uses only exact-case `text` keys.
findings.citation: Go go1.27.1 src/encoding/json/decode.go:700-703 (byFoldedName match); RULEBOOK §2 ('a reviewer who sees an unlisted construct flags it for this table'); inventory.tsv row websearch/cloud/service.go 'snippetFromContent' [WIRE]

findings.finding: Decode success/failure flip, unflagged by row or code: Go decodes with json.NewDecoder(...).Decode, which 'reads the next JSON-encoded value from its input' (encoding/json/stream.go:46) — a 200 body of `{"results":[]}garbage` DECODES SUCCESSFULLY in Go (trailing bytes ignored), while the port's `resp.json()` -> json.loads raises JSONDecodeError 'Extra data' (probed). The two WIRE-DECODE rows only waive the error-message TEXT on malformed bodies ('the port lets resp.json() raise — message text differs... unjudged'); neither contemplates the case where Go succeeds and the port raises, which for websearch is a publicly reachable tool error (NIL-ERR row: decode failure surfaces as the tool error). No fixture exercises it; the impl followed the row — this is an inventory blind spot to flag under §5.
findings.citation: Go go1.27.1 src/encoding/json/stream.go:46; inventory.tsv WIRE-DECODE rows (websearch/cloud/output.go, webfetch/cloud/output.go) + NIL-ERR row (':104-107 JSON decode failure re-raise'); RULEBOOK §5

findings.finding: Latent Protocol/concrete signature clash picked silently: the IFACE row pins the Protocol as `def fetch(self, url: str, opts: FetchOpts) -> FetchResult`, while the CTX row pins the cloud concrete as `def fetch(self, target_url: str, ...)`. The impl (line 46) uses `target_url` and records no marker. mypy strict Protocol checking requires matching parameter names for positional-or-keyword params, so once webfetch/service.py is written per the IFACE row, CloudWebFetchService.fetch will not satisfy WebFetchService — a cross-row conflict the implementer resolved by silently choosing one side (no TODO(port)). The websearch twin is consistent (`input` on both rows), which shows this is not a general convention.
findings.citation: inventory.tsv row internal/services/webfetch/service.go 'WebFetchService' [IFACE] ('def fetch(self, url: str, opts: FetchOpts)') vs row 'CloudWebFetchService.Fetch (site 29) + makeRequest' [CTX] ('def fetch(self, target_url: str, ...)'); impl service.py:46

findings.finding: Impl deviates from the row's letter in Go's favor (should be row-amended, not code-fixed): the snippetFromContent row's dict branch reads 'parsed is dict and parsed.get("text") truthy -> that text', which for content `{"text":true}` would return Python True; the impl (lines 174-175) requires `isinstance(text, str) and text != ""`, which is what Go does (Unmarshal of a bool into the struct's string field errors -> raw echo; probed: impl('{"text":true}') = '{"text":true}'). A divergence from the inventory row as written, reported so the row text gets corrected.
findings.citation: inventory.tsv row websearch/cloud/service.go 'snippetFromContent' [WIRE] ('parsed is dict and parsed.get("text") truthy'); Go internal/services/websearch/cloud/service.go:125 (`err == nil && obj.Text != ""` with string-typed field)

findings.finding: Cosmetic §4-letter divergence in import form: §4 prescribes 'import the sibling module and qualify — `from websearch.services.websearch.cloud import output` then `output.Output`'. Both files instead import the symbols directly (`from websearch.services.webfetch.cloud.output import Output`, webfetch line 18; `from websearch.services.websearch.cloud.output import Output`, websearch line 22) even while the websearch docstring claims 'module-qualified imports, §4'. The intent (absolute, unambiguous, no relative/star imports — verified none) is met; the prescribed qualify-the-module form is not followed for output/parameters (network and the sibling service module do use module+alias form).
findings.citation: RULEBOOK §4 ('import the sibling module and qualify... Never relative imports, never star imports'); impl websearch service.py:21-23, webfetch service.py:16-19

findings.finding: Cosmetic: the Go deref `performRequest(*s.cfg.HTTPClient, request)` (service.go:59) panics on a nil client; the port mirrors it with `assert client is not None` (line 69), which `python -O` strips, degrading to an AttributeError inside client.send instead. The CALL-BY-VALUE/NIL-ZERO rows mandate 'the stored client is non-Optional after new()' but prescribe no mechanism; noting the -O gap only because the assert is the sole guard.
findings.citation: Go internal/services/webfetch/cloud/service.go:59 and internal/services/websearch/cloud/service.go:51; inventory.tsv CALL-BY-VALUE + NIL-ZERO rows; impl webfetch service.py:67-70, websearch service.py:67-71

adherence: Did the implementer follow the rulebook? Per-site, in the two cloud service.py files: YES, unusually faithfully — every checked site traces to a named inventory row and to the Go source. Verified clean: guard order and byte-exact guard strings (webfetch 'url must not be empty' before 'base_url must not be empty'; websearch 'query must not be empty' §2-pinned, with the correct asymmetry that websearch has NO base_url guard and none was added); format default to 'markdown'; omitempty body construction exactly per parameters.go (max_results iff != 0, country/language iff non-empty, model/query always; webfetch model/url/format always with format's dead omitempty correctly reasoned); FF-3 correct at BOTH sites (webfetch kept-conditional per Go:93-95, websearch implements the fix per §0 FF-3 — header absent on empty key, 'Bearer ' byte-exact otherwise); _join_url_path matches the URL-JOIN row's pinned Go probe matrix 14/14 (probed) with urljoin correctly banned; DefaultClient fallback wiring exactly per the NIL-ZERO/NIL-DEFAULT rows (network.new_client(os.environ.get('HTTPS_PROXY','')), dataclasses.replace mirroring Go's value-copy cfg, no bare httpx.Client); DEFER-CLOSE recipe per row (send, reads in try, finally close, no stream=True); CALL-BY-VALUE site by-reference per row; ERR-ORDER non-replication satisfied (websearch builds httpx.Request — which raises at construction — before any header set; webfetch needs nothing special); full uncapped error body at the webfetch ERR-STRING site (the 5 MB cap is grabber-only); results list-comprehension never None (s17); no ctx params anywhere in all three files; no relative/star imports; no type:ignore/cast/Any (§3 clean); TODO(port) markers well-formed and §6 trailers honest (3/2/2 TODOs match the trailers). The failure is at the tree/process level, not the site level: (1) the batch is unimportable — 8 manifest-listed sibling modules are absent from src/ and the §1-sanctioned runtime deps (httpx, beautifulsoup4) are undeclared (`dependencies = []`, nothing in uv.lock/venv), so §0's mandatory `make lint typecheck` referee cannot have passed, and §7 logs no deviation (DEV-001..004 cover other things) while both cloud files claim confidence=high; (2) two silent Go-semantics gaps that neither the code nor the inventory rows decide: encoding/json's case-insensitive struct-field matching (content {\"Text\":\"hi\"} -> Go \"hi\" vs port raw echo; decode.go:700-703) and json.Decoder.Decode's first-value-only read (trailing garbage succeeds in Go, raises 'Extra data' in the port; stream.go:46) — both flag-worthy under §2's reviewer obligation. Plus one latent cross-row conflict adopted silently (Protocol `url` vs concrete `target_url` in the fetch signature) and two cosmetic letter-of-the-row nits. Fix-forward posture: the code sites themselves are obedient; what is missing is the referee run, the sibling units the batch depends on, and an honest confidence=low or a §7 line saying the referee was waived for this round.
